Thank you for coming to the aid of Yipe!  We are in desperate need of your help!  Strange monsters have been attacking the innocent people of Yipe!  Even worse, my collection of six rare stamps has been stolen!

Last time I talked to you I got a little carried away.  I forgot to mention the other problem I have.  All of my daughters are missing!  I figure that some were kidnapped, others are lost, and some just ran away.  Unfortunately, I forget how many I have.
Wow!  You have found one of my rare stamps!  I only need five more before my life can return to normal.  Have you tried searching in any of the other caves around the world?
Thank you for trying to help the town.  I am totally unable to rule as King without my stamps.  Of course, it would also be nice to have all my daughters back.
You've done well in the quests that I have given you.  Keep up your good work and I'm sure that Yipe! will return to its normal peaceful state.

Thank you for returning me some of the princesses!  It sure is much more pleasant having my daughters running around the castle again!  One daughter has told me that there are many more still in need of rescuing.

Three stamps!  You have returned half of my stamps to me!  This is cause for celebration!  I will organize a party tonight in your honor.  But, don't get too carried away, there are still more stamps to find!
It seems that each main cave holds one of my rare stamps.  There must be more caves somewhere out in the world of Yipe!  Have you searched everywhere?  Oh how I long to have my precious stamps back!

Thank you so much for saving around 10 of my daughters.  They tell me that there are still many more of their sisters around the world.  One princess suggested that I give you my lucky rabbit foot to help you out.
You have returned to me five of my rare stamps!  There is only one stamp left out there!  I pray that it is not lost or too hard to find.  If you can't find it I don't think anyone can do it.
The cave directly to the east of Yipe! is probably the next best place to look for another one of my rare stamps.  You probably are not strong enough to explore the rest of the world.

I have heard rumors that a huge monster lives deep in the cave that is located right here in the town of Yipe!  Perhaps somewhere beyond this monster may be the answers to finding my stamps and daughters.
I have been told that the entrance to the final cave is in the middle of a tall mountain range.  The only way to enter is through a portal that appears near a group of small rocks.
I wish that I could follow you into the caves and seek revenge on these evil monsters myself.  However, I am old and not as strong as you are.  It is up to you to find the last few remaining stamps!
You are truly a brave adventurer!  I thank you for everything that you have done for me and the entire city of Yipe!

Ah ha... I see you found the water proof shoe spray.  Did you know that with the spray you will be able to cross over certain streams around the world?  I hear north of Yipe! there is another cave surrounding by water.

Four stamps!  It is soooo great to have almost all of my stamps back.  Have you been checking all the treasure chests you find along the way?  You may need some of the items you find in the chests to be able to find the rest of my stamps.
The Gatekeeper is responsible!  I should have known someone living in Hell must be evil!  Did you know there is more than one way to enter Hell?  One doesn't have to die to get there.
Holy Cow!  You have returned all six stamps to me.  This is perhaps the best day of my life!  Well... it might be another good day if you could return all my daughters to me.
Congratulations!  You have defeated the evil Gatekeeper!  I'm sure the world will soon be peaceful once again.  Now, if only you could find the rest of my daughters for me.

All of my princesses are back and happily living in the castle!  You have also killed off the evil gatekeeper and returned all my stamps!  Our world is now peaceful, however take this weapon and armor as my thanks to you.
Those princesses sure are hard to find.  Have you looked for secret walls?  Sailed all the rafts?  Looked behind every door?  Fallen through traps?  Who knows where they all might be.

How strange!  There is a stamp stuck to the back of your armor.  You must have found one of my rare stamps somewhere in one of the caves.  I guess it ended up sticking to you before you had a chance to find it.
If you are bored of fighting monsters and searching for stamps and princesses, perhaps you could spend some time at the Yipe! casino.  It is located just a short distance from my castle.
One of the townsfolk recently escaped from the cave here in town.  He told me a huge monster at the very end of the cave was holding something small and square.

It seems that only the largest of the monsters in this world are holding stamps.  You'll need more protection to kill these larger monsters.  Try equiping yourself with helmets, gloves, boots and magical rings.

Two caves fully explored and two stamps found.  Only seems logical that the next cave will have another stamp of mine.  Have I ever shown you the current value of my stamps in the latest Stamp Price Guide?
There is a post-it note on the King's throne.  A servant named Eric takes the note and walks it over to you.  The note says:
Wow!  You have found two of my rare stamps!  You seem to have a great knack for finding rare stamps!  I only need four more before my life can return to normal.
I hear that you have defeated the gatekeeper in the past.  Remember that each time you defeat him, he grows stronger.  Make sure to carry lots of healing potions before dealing with him again!
One of my daughters told me that her younger sister is still missing.  She also tells me that this missing princess was very fond of water.  Perhaps she wandered north into the water cave?
Still looking for princesses?  When I wanted to hide from the world I used to enter the stone cave, go north, go past a door and through a secret wall.  Maybe try looking there?
Is there something I can help you with?  I'm really quite busy playing with my entire stamp collection.  Maybe you could go catch a bunny for my daughters to play with.
An assistant to the King comes out and tells you that until a new problem arises in the world of Yipe! that the King has no need for your services.
Please, help me find my stamps!
Find them, and I shall reward you!
Here is 500 gold to reward you for your good deeds!
I wish you luck my friend.
We all owe you greatly for your good deeds.
Princesses are well known for hiding in tricky spots.
The King give you 1000 gold coins!
The breeding grounds are not one of the main caves.
The King gives you his Lucky Rabbit Foot.
The King looks hopefully at you.
You must first travel south, then east, and then north to reach the cave.
I hope you don't give up.  The city is counting on you!
I wish I could help you more myself.
You might need to climb over a tree or cross a stream.
Take this 5000 gold pieces as a token of my gratitude.

Try walking into all the walls.  You might be able to go through some.
Thanks for finding another rare stamp!

You can purchase some of these things in some of the shops.
This might be a good time to sneak out of the castle.
Here is 500 gold to reward you for your good deeds!
Spell point healing potions can only be purchased in Quizilog.
You don't need a boat to travel to some areas of the water cave.
One time I even saw a princess blessing the water in that room.
You have completed everything in Yipe! III
I guess you'll have to wait for Yipe! IV...

Quest of Yipe! III

  The city of Yipe! has become wealthy and prosperous.  Many people consider Yipe! their beloved home, including you.  Unfortunately, many bad things have happened to the innocent city over the years.  At one point an evil wizard trapped the town with landslides; another time the city was out of simple supplies like food and water. But, as the sign of a great city, Yipe! has fought and grown stronger rather than become a ghost town.

  Over the past few months there have been reports of more and more monster attacks in the areas around Yipe!  The beautiful caves normally used for shelter and exploration appear to be the homeland of these awful monsters.

Knowing that you are a brave adventurer, the King has once again come to you for help.  The King's rare stamp collection has been stolen.  This collection of six stamps is very dear to the King.  He believes the sudden increase in the monster population and the disappearance of his stamps is no coincidence.

  On a side note, the King also informs you that all of his daughters are missing.  He thinks that the monsters may have kidnapped some of them, while others may have run away or are just lost.  The King is not really sure how many daughters he has, but will reward you if you can ever find them all.  (Only the daughters themselves will know when you rescue them all.)

The King will give you a simple weapon and piece of armor along with a warm hat to get you started.  He suggests that you start looking in the cave that is located right next to the city of Yipe!  Follow the path from the town buildings across the small bridge and into this normally peaceful cave.

  The King tells you that there are many caves located throughout the world.  There are also other towns that might carry special items that Yipe! does not produce.  He warns you of a place called Yipe! Hell where a gatekeeper charges a fee to return wounded adventurers.

  You must now choose what type of character you would like to use in Quest of Yipe! III.

The new character setup window allows you to start creating a new adventurer.  You have the choice of three different pre-set characters, or you can build your own.

  The three types are: Combat, Quickness, and Magic.
  While you are in this window, click on any of the types to find out more information on that particular type.
  In general, all different types of characters are of equal ability.

  Once you have selected your character type you will go on to the next window.  From here you should first select what difficulty level you want and then pick what you want your character to look like.

Strength (Str):  The stronger you are the more likely you will hit your enemies.  You will also hit for more damage as you gain strength.  If you selected the 'Combat' type of character, you will be more likely to gain strength.

  Dexterity (Dex):  Dexterity represents how agile and quick you are.  The higher this stat is the harder it will be for monsters to hit you.  Dexterity is also used with some of the special abilities (talked about later).  The 'Quickness' type of character relies on this stat.

  Intelligence (Int):  This stat is important for casting spells.  The higher this stat is the more powerful your spells will be.  Intelligence is also used when using special potions and in all aspects of healing.  The 'Magic' type of character will want a high intelligence.

Level:  This is a representation of how powerful your character is.  In the beginning you will start out as a level one adventurer.  The only way to raise this stat is by killing monsters and gaining experience.

  Experience (Exp):  You will gain experience for each monster you kill.  The harder the monster is to kill the more experience you will earn.  After you gain a certain amount of Exp, your level will increase.

  Kills:  This is a count of how many times you have killed each type of monster.  It is just for your information.  The list of kills is in order of how powerful each monster is, except for the final monsters, which are all listed at the end.
  If you have not actually gone into combat with a particular monster you will see '?????' in the place of where the monster's name will go in the kills list.

You can use the mouse button to move around the world.  Your character will always try to move in the direction that you click the mouse.  You don't have to click right next to the character for him/her to move.

  You can also use the keyboard to move around.  Use the 'Set Keys...' option from the menu bar to pick the keys you want to use to move around.  The number pad can always be used to move your character around (with NUM Lock on).

  Your character can walk through most areas of the game.  You can't walk on water,  mountains, trees, and cave walls.  Be careful of what you walk on in the caves!

Sometimes you will see a chest on the ground.  Walk into it to open up the chest and you will receive whatever treasure is inside.

  There are also signs in certain places.  Just walk onto the sign to read it.  The information that is on the sign will be displayed on the lower left hand side of the main window.

  You can find out a little more information about most of the different types of terrain in the game.  For example, try clicking the 'Other' button when you are standing on a flower.  In the same area that the signs are displayed (the lower left hand side of the main window), you will see a short message about what you are standing on.

You can equip yourself with several different types of items.  If you press the 'Stats' button on the lower left section of the main screen and then press the 'Equipment' button you will see a list of all the types of items you can use.  (For quick access to this list you can select it from the menu bar, or type 'Ctrl' E).

  The two main things you need are a sturdy weapon and some solid body armor.  You can find these items for sale in the shops in town.  You will also find a monster carrying an item you can use from time to time.  When you go back to a shop after finding new items, the shop owner will automatically pay you for your old items.  Generally in a shop, the more expensive the item is, the better it is.

The other types of items you can wear are:  helmets, gloves, rings, amulets, and boots.  You can find a few of these items in the miscellaneous shop in town.  These items primarily provide you with protection from monsters.  A few special items help protect you and help you attack.  You will notice in the 'Equipment' list, each item has a WC and an AC number.

	     WC = Weapon class.  (As this increases you will be more likely to hit a monster)
	     AC = Armor class.  (The higher this is the less likely a monster will hit you) 

  You will find other types of items in the game that are not for armor or fighting.  These include healing items and other types of special magic potions.

There are a few special types of items that don't fall into any of the other categories.

  At some point you will stumble upon a door.  Many of the doors are unlocked and just waiting for you to open them up.  However, some doors are locked with one of the two types of keys in the world of Yipe!  Somewhere in the game you will find these keys.

  Other special items that you may collect later will help you get to places that you could not reach before.  For instance, you may be able to cross streams or climb certain trees with the special items that you find.
  These special items are not always that easy to find.

There are four main types of shops.  These include:  A weapon shop, an armor shop, a healing shop, and a miscellaneous shop.

  The weapon and armor shops both list the available weapons or armors for sale.  Before you purchase a new item you must first sell your old weapon or armor.  Note the WC or AC values to the side of each number.  When you go to buy a new item make sure it has a higher WC or AC than the item you already have.

  The healing shop sells four food items.  The more expensive the food item, the more points your character will be healed.  Note:  There are no 'Take Out' orders available from the healing shops.

The last main shop type is the miscellaneous shop.  This shop carries all sorts of random items.  Items available include everything from healing items that can be taken with you to potions for scaring off monsters or returning you to the surface.  Some of these miscellaneous shops carry items that you can wear.  For instance, they might sell a very powerful helmet or amulet.

  There are a few other types of buildings you will find along your journey.  In the main town of Yipe! there is the spell hut.  There are also specialty buildings in some of the caves.  Both of these types of buildings will be talked about later.

  There is also a Yipe! Casino that is located fairly close to the main town.

After you have equipped yourself, you are ready to go out and kill some evil monsters.  In the beginning look for the little bunnies and then the cave beetles.

  To attack the monsters just walk into them.  At this point a new window will come up with a picture of the monster(s), a picture of you, and the health information about all of you.  If there is more than 1 monster attacking you, you can click on the picture of the one you want to attack first.

  Now press the attack button or press the attack key (initially set to 'a').  You get the first attack, and then each monster still alive on the screen gets one shot at you.  You can take as long as you want to attack.

There are five different options for you while you are attacking.  As mentioned above, you can attack the monster by hitting the attack button.  You can also cast spells, try to run away, use an item, and later in the game, use special abilities.

  Hit the cast button or press the cast key (initially set to 'c') to cast a spell.  More info on spells later.

  Hit the run button or press the run key (initially set to 'r') to try to run away.  Sometimes a monster won't let you run away, but you can keep trying until you escape.  Beware:  if the monster doesn't let you run, it still gets a chance to hit you.

Hit the 'items' button or press the items key (initially set to 'i') to use an item.  You may use one item per attack round.

  Once you learn a special ability a new button will appear in your attack window.  Hit this button to use your special attack.  Or press the special ability key (initially set to 's').  Special abilities will be talked about later.

  After you have killed all the enemies in the attack window a message will pop up telling you how much gold and experience you have collected.  A new button will appear that says 'Done'.  Hit this button or press the 'Enter' or 'Return' key to exit the attack window and return to the main window.

You can learn spells from the magic temple in the main town.  As you become more experienced you will be able to learn more powerful spells.

  Epiy is the town wizard.  In his temple you can heal your spell points and learn new spells.  Your spell points will gradually heal over time, or you can pay Epiy to heal them for you.  There is a rumor that some store sells a spell point potion that can heal your spell points.

  Each spell has a low power and high power setting.  With attacking spells, a low power spell will hit only the monster you are currently attacking.  A high power spell will hit all the monsters on the screen.  For healing spells, the high power just increases the amount of healing you receive.

In the spells window you will notice a 'Status' area for each spell on the far right hand side.  This tells you when you will be able to cast certain spells.

  The three status options are:  Combat, Either, and Non-Combat.  Either means you can cast the spell either in combat or while exploring.  Non-Combat spells are only allowed to be cast while exploring.  For instance the 'Return to Surface' spell is a Non-Combat spell.  Finally, combat means the spell can only be cast while fighting.

  High power spells will cost twice as much to cast as low power.  If the cost doesn't change when you switch to high power, the spell has the same effect for both power levels.

There are four different special abilities that your character will be able to learn throughout the game.  You will find shops in certain caves that can train your character in one of the abilities.

  Your character can only know one ability at a time.  However, you are free to learn one ability and then go back and relearn an old ability that you used to know.  Typically, the more dangerous caves will contain more powerful abilities.

  The first ability you will encounter is the 'Backstab'.  When you use this ability your character will sneak around the first monster in the combat window and stab them causing a certain amount of damage.  The backstab has a greater affect against more powerful enemies.

Your character will have either 5 or 6 maximum ability points (AP) at the start of the game.  The cost to use an ability is always 3 AP.  There are very few ways to heal your ability points.

  The most common way for your AP to heal is through time.  As time passes while you are exploring the world your AP will slowly regenerate.  It is also possible that a princess might heal your ability points.  There is no way to ever increase your AP past 6 points.

  One benefit of using a special ability is that when you use it, none of the monsters in the attack window will get to attack you during the round that you used your ability.

In the shops:
  The escape (Esc) key will exit the shop.
  The up and down arrow keys can be used to move up and down the list of items for sale.

Attacking:
  After you have killed all the enemies, the Enter or Esc key will bring you out of attack mode.
  The left and right arrow keys can be used to switch which monter you are currently attacking when you are fighting more than one at a time.

Movement:
  You don't need to set keys to use the number pad to move around.

Keyboard commands can be changed from the options menu: 'Edit Keyboard Commands...'

This game is shareware.  That means if you like it you must pay for it.  Paying for shareware games inspires me to continue programming.

  Then again, you don't have to.  The first part of this game is free.  Unfortunately you won't be able to finish the game unless you register.

  With an unregistered copy, you will be able to explore the entire first three caves.  You will also be able to explore part of the fourth cave.

  With partial registration, you will be able to explore the rest of cave four as well as cave five.  With full registration you can explore the entire world as well as be able to complete the game and register your high score.

I like to give people an option for payment since not everyone has the same budget.

  These first few levels of price all include:

  The full registration code for Yipe! III.  The code will be either emailed to you or sent in a letter if you don't have email access.

$5 -  This game needs lots of improvements... (or I am really broke)
$6 -  Nice game.  The game is entertaining... but needs a little more.
$7 -  Great game!  Continue making Quest of Yipe! games.

  If you have registered for previous Yipe! games you may cut the above prices in half.

The following registration payments include:
